purpose: Keep supervisor diagnostics off the deadline-owning thread with a bounded lossy queue.
behavior: Retains at most 32 queued lines, drops the newest line on overflow and accumulates a dropped-line count.
A helper drains a line with its accumulated drop count, writes a prefixed diagnostic and optional drop notice, and ignores write/flush errors.
Mutex and condition-variable poisoning recover the contained state rather than panicking.
contracts: The control path only enqueues; it never writes host stderr.
dependencies: channel::helper supplies the drain thread; tree.rs reports incomplete member proofs through Diag.
failures_or_limits: A blocked sink can hold the helper forever and diagnostics can be lost; queue capacity bounds line count rather than String byte size. report still takes a short mutex, so its never-blocks comment means no blocking sink I/O, not lock-free execution.

purpose: Return live Windows Job inventory while distinguishing unknown observations from departed members.
behavior: Obtains Job candidate PIDs, excludes an exited root, opens each candidate and verifies Job membership before reading metadata.
Holds verified process handles through a ToolHelp snapshot, rechecks liveness, and obtains creation times for entries that remain.
Includes parentPid only when the parent is also listed and no younger than the child; empty executable names become None.
contracts: Query/snapshot failures propagate as incomplete inventory rather than an empty success.
dependencies: job.rs supplies member_pids/probe/exited; tree.rs returns results through List/Processes or Ack::Error.
failures_or_limits: The snapshot is not an atomic process-tree view; members absent from it or exited by the later check are omitted. HashMap iteration gives no stable order, and names are lossy UTF-16 conversions.

purpose: Own the Windows Job kill boundary and conservative PID membership probes.
behavior: Creates an anonymous noninheritable Job with only KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, never a breakaway flag.
Queries active/total counts as Option, lists member PIDs with four bounded growth retries, and reports listing failure as unknown.
Probes a PID through an owned query/synchronize handle and distinguishes Gone, Outside and Member; only ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER means no process.
Forced termination uses exit code one; a failed call is left for repeated tree settlement passes.
contracts: Unknown active counts are not zero in the normal Tree proof; a retained Member handle pins the observed process identity.
dependencies: tree.rs repeats termination and owns the Job; members.rs/inventory.rs consume conservative probes.
failures_or_limits: terminate ignores its immediate API result and requires the caller to observe completion. Active count zero alone precedes the stronger per-member proof. container/mod.rs has a separate bounded polling policy that does accept unknown as a break condition.

purpose: Track Windows Job births and prove departure after an empty Job flushes its completion notifications.
behavior: Associates the completion port before processes exist and records NEW_PROCESS PIDs plus an unswept notification total; periodic sweeps prune certainly-gone identities.
Once empty, posts a marker, waits until seen, reconciles notification total against Job TotalProcesses and unions any remaining listed PIDs.
Each candidate must be gone, outside the Job, or signalled; a live member is Pending and query/accounting/notification gaps are Unknown.
The completion worker wakes the owner on empty and flush events; a port failure leaves proofs unresolved.
contracts: Members::prove must be called only after the Job is confirmed empty.
dependencies: job.rs supplies counts/probes; queues.rs carries Settle; tree.rs owns the final proof deadline and result policy.
failures_or_limits: The stronger proof is not an unconditional Stopped prerequisite: tree.rs permits Pending/Unknown after one second of confirmed emptiness, with a diagnostic. Embedded hooks suppress a birth or blind a probe for tests, not production recovery.

purpose: Run the Windows supervisor owner loop with request admission, deadline enforcement and host-loss cleanup.
behavior: Enforces tree deadlines before waiting and again before handling one queued item; events take precedence through Inbox, and polling runs every 10 ms while stopping or 100 ms for lingering roots.
Admits requests only below the owed-reply budget, preserves released tombstones until gone, rejects requests to unknown/released IDs and refuses spawns at the tree limit.
Registers Job membership before process creation, arms an exit watcher before publishing Spawned, and rolls failed setup back by dropping the owned Job.
Host loss closes queues, starts each live tree stop with its own grace, and exits success when all are gone or failure at the longest remaining deadline plus five seconds.
contracts: Go is a Windows no-op for known trees; Stop replies await Tree settlement, not root exit alone.
dependencies: boot/channel/queues provide transport; spawn/tree/members own process state; diag avoids owner-thread stderr I/O.
failures_or_limits: A too-large process list yields Ack::Error; other unencodable replies or queue overflow trigger host loss. Normal protocol deadlines do not make synchronous OS spawn/inventory calls interruptible.

purpose: Bound Windows owner requests and owed replies while reserving capacity for lifecycle events.
behavior: Allows 64 queued requests and blocks only the reader at that limit; HostGone is deduplicated and lifecycle events are taken ahead of requests.
Admission elsewhere counts 1024 outstanding replies/Stop waiters; capacity additionally reserves one Exited per 4096 trees plus Ready.
Outbox counts frames already taken by the writer until written, batches queued bytes for the writer, and refuses overflow without blocking the owner.
Closing Inbox drops pending requests and wakes the reader; closing Outbox discards queued frames and wakes its drain.
contracts: Events rely on one root-exit and bounded settle notifications per tree for their construction bound.
dependencies: mod.rs enforces reply/tree admission; channel.rs performs blocking reads/writes and reports progress.
failures_or_limits: Bounds count requests/frames rather than bytes, with individual message size bounded by the protocol. No writer-progress timeout is implemented here; owner deadlines continue because the writer is independent.

purpose: Validate Windows spawn wire data, consume transferred stdio and create a contained pipe or terminal root.
behavior: Takes ownership of each distinct transferred pipe once, refuses repeated/missing/extra slots and never adopts the channel or non-pipe values; closed stdin becomes a readable NUL handle.
Requires valid NUL-free WTF-8 and an absolute program, checks cwd metadata, resolves batch scripts through the system-directory cmd.exe and refuses batch or extra argv with verbatim mode.
Builds a double-NUL environment block with ASCII-case sorting, creates/watches a Job before the root, and optionally creates ConPTY before CreateProcessW.
Maps common Windows errors to NotFound, NotExecutable or BadCwd and returns owned handles so failed setup closes containment.
contracts: The launch path never resolves cmd.exe through PATH or ComSpec; HANDLE_LIST/PSEUDOCONSOLE plus JOB_LIST are delegated to create.rs.
dependencies: cmdline.rs quoting/WTF-8; pty_windows.rs console lifetime; job.rs containment; host spawn/env.rs prepares environment.
failures_or_limits: Environment sorting here folds only ASCII, whereas the host environment name helper folds BMP letters; equivalence for non-ASCII names is not established. Transferred-handle ownership assumes a cooperating authenticated host, not arbitrary valid pipe-handle numbers.
